solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It hurts to block relative almost free of habit

indicators.note: the cry is put in the way of the relative, sitting inside it
almost means the relative's last letter is dropped

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
OW is the cry that says it hurts

explanation.surface: A painful complaint about a relative who is somehow nearly free of a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The habit is a monk's garment, not an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncowl is to remove a monk's hood, so one uncowled is stripped of that part of the religious habit.

clue.text: Where men go to let out new sheep

indicators.note: letting out releases a letter, removing it from the word

parts.note: a urinal is a gents' convenience

explanation.surface: Men head to the toilet to let out some sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' suggests relieving oneself, but it drops the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The urial is a wild sheep of Central and South Asia with large curled horns.

clue.text: Stiff chap in Bentley?

indicators.note: in puts the chap inside the vehicle

parts.note: a Bentley is an example of a car, flagged by the question mark
Dave is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A stuffy gentleman sitting in his Bentley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like a starchy upright gent, but it is slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, which slang calls a stiff.

clue.text: Casanova runs after a winsome wanton

indicators.note: after places the R behind the rearranged letters
wanton means unruly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Casanova pursues an attractive, promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was a famous seducer, and his name now stands for any serial seducer of women.

clue.text: Torment of Sahara's sands

indicators.note: of says the answer is taken from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the apostrophe-s and into the next word

explanation.surface: The torment of trudging through desert sand.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside saHARA'S Sands.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to pester and badger them persistently, a verb sense shared exactly.

clue.text: Maiden is more lovely without top

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter goes

parts.note: fairer means more beautiful

explanation.surface: A girl grows prettier when she takes her top off.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern English dialect a maiden is a clothes-horse for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is a dialect name for a clothes-horse, a frame on which laundry is dried.

clue.text: Clobber sappers in disgust

indicators.note: in puts the sappers inside the word for disgust

parts.note: to appal is to disgust
sappers are the Royal Engineers, RE

explanation.surface: Army engineers are disgusted at someone's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes and gear, not a verb for hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British for clothing, as is apparel.

clue.text: Cook oranges regularly with southern wine

parts.note: to saute is to cook by frying quickly

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of oranges

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook oranges with a southern dessert wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: After review, small medical bill reduced for third party

indicators.note: a review looks back, so the whole collection is read backwards

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: reduced means the bill loses its last letter

parts.note: a bill is an invoice, here BILL as written

explanation.surface: A medical bill that, after review, was cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: S, MED and BIL are joined and 'After review' turns the lot round. The Liberal Democrats were long Britain's third-largest party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal Democrats were traditionally the third force in British politics behind Labour and the Conservatives.

clue.text: Deadbeat doctor unconscious behind surgery

indicators.note: behind places the word for unconscious after the earlier parts

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation
someone knocked out is out cold

explanation.surface: A doctor who is out cold behind the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropout is someone who has quit conventional society, a shiftless idler or layabout.

clue.text: Name at end of letter tearing us apart

indicators.note: torn apart, the letters are pulled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A letter signed off with a name is breaking a couple apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is the writer's own name signed by hand at the foot of a letter.

clue.text: Less careful solver recklessly snorting fresh line

indicators.note: snorting means taking in, so one group of letters goes inside the other
recklessly says the letters of solver are thrown about
fresh signals the letters of line are made anew in a new order

explanation.surface: A careless crossword solver snorting a line of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Both anagrams are done first; 'snorting' then puts the reworked line inside the reworked solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenly means untidy and careless, so the comparative is more slapdash.

clue.text: Regretted sounding vulgar

indicators.note: sounding says the word for vulgar is heard, not spelt

parts.note: rude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone regretting having sounded coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rued is the past tense of rue, an old verb for feeling sorrow or remorse.

clue.text: Manx cat fed by bishop sounds contented

indicators.note: fed by means something is put into the cat
a Manx cat has no tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: puss is a cat
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A tailless Manx cat, given food by a bishop, purrs happily.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat is a breed born without a tail, so 'Manx' docks the last letter; Right Reverend is a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat purrs, making a low vibrating hum that shows it is content.

clue.text: Commonplace introduction to poetic licence

indicators.note: introduction means take the first letter

parts.note: first letter of poetic
latitude is freedom or licence

explanation.surface: The phrase 'poetic licence' is itself a commonplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, a commonplace said too often to mean much.

clue.text: Little person cuddling up

definitions.meaning: a baby bird still in the nest, or a small child

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a noun for a tiny one and a verb form for snuggling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a fledgling bird, and nestling is also the present participle of nestle, to snuggle close.

clue.text: Speciousness of fool with loveless past

parts.note: a sop is a feeble or foolish person

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O goes

parts.note: history is the past

explanation.surface: An idiot with a past bereft of love is speciously reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love means zero, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophistry is clever but deceptive reasoning, an argument that only seems sound.

clue.text: Dance with a cad in Australian town

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
a rat is a cad, a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Dancing with a scoundrel in an Australian town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ballarat is a city in Victoria, famous for its gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballarat is a regional city in Victoria, Australia, founded in the gold rush of the 1850s.

clue.text: Freckles from time in Foreign Legion

indicators.note: in puts the time inside the rearranged letters
foreign suggests something altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Time spent in the Foreign Legion leaves someone freckled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign Legion' reads as one unit, but 'Foreign' signals the anagram of LEGION.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is the medical term for small pigmented spots on the skin such as freckles.

clue.text: Boozer vacuously exposes nether regions

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

indicators.note: vacuously means emptied, keeping only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of exposes

explanation.surface: A drunk flashes his private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer here is a pub, not a drinker; 'vacuously' empties EXPOSES to ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The pubes are the lower front of the abdomen, the genital region euphemistically called the nether regions.

clue.text: Reportedly somewhat poor and surly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word for poor is heard rather than seen

parts.note: bare means poor, lacking
the suffix -ish means somewhat

explanation.surface: Someone said to be rather poor and bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearish means grumpy and rough-mannered, like a bear with a sore head.

clue.text: Sibelius perhaps beginning to nod after bit of fish

indicators.note: after places the first letter of nod behind the fin

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter

parts.note: first letter of nod

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off after a bite of fish, with Sibelius somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Sibelius was a Finnish composer, hence a Finn; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius was born in Finland, so he is one example of a native of that country.

clue.text: Shoots as regiment runs amok

indicators.note: running amok is wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Soldiers shoot as their regiment goes on a rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' looks like gunfire but is the verb for sprouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant shoots when it sprouts, and a seed germinates when it starts to grow.

clue.text: Sentimental fling after finally ditching beau

indicators.note: after places the throw word behind the two final letters
finally means take the last letter of each word

parts.note: last letter of ditching
last letter of beau
to shy is to throw or fling

explanation.surface: A sentimental fling ends with a boyfriend getting dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' looks like a romance but means a throw; 'finally' picks G and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushy describes effusive, overly emotional talk, sentimental to excess.

clue.text: Mendicant disregarding black moth

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out a letter

parts.note: a mendicant is a beggar
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A beggar ignores a black moth.
explanation.definitionFit: The eggar is a large brown moth of the family Lasiocampidae, such as the oak eggar.

clue.text: Technology's magic is tackling and fighting system

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so the magic word takes the other inside

parts.note: juju is West African magic or a charm
IT is information technology, plus the 's

explanation.surface: The magic of technology tackles a martial art.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is the usual crossword shorthand for information technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Jujitsu is a Japanese martial art of unarmed combat built on throws and holds.

clue.text: Tough guy heartlessly hounding half-cut playwright

indicators.note: hounding means chasing, so the guy follows behind the playwright
half-cut means only the front half of the name is kept

parts.note: August Strindberg was a Swedish playwright

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: GUY as written

explanation.surface: A man without heart pursues a drunk playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like British slang for drunk, but here it cuts the Swedish dramatist's ten-letter surname in half; 'hounding' sets the guy behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringy meat is fibrous and chewy, which is to say tough.

clue.text: Some mediocre pony missing the Derby?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An average pony that fails to run in the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby horse race is named after the Earl of Derby, so the race is an example of something taking a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a thing named after a person, and the Derby race bears the name of the 12th Earl of Derby.

clue.text: Case of Chardonnay initially pleases female nonentity

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Chardonnay

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

parts.note: first letter of pleases
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A case of wine pleases a woman, yet she counts for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypher (cipher) is a person of no importance, a mere zero.
